summary: Omega-3 fatty acids include ALA, EPA and DHA and contribute to cell membranes. These forms are not interchangeable intake targets.

functions.title: Physiological role
functions.description: Omega-3 fatty acids include ALA, EPA and DHA and contribute to cell membranes. These forms are not interchangeable intake targets.

foodSourceRules.notes: Total omega-3 composition is unavailable; individual ALA, EPA and DHA values are not inferred or conflated.

absorptionFactors.description: The body converts only small amounts of ALA to EPA and DHA. No conversion percentage or total omega-3 composition is inferred.

deficiency.overview: ODS describes deficiency as rare in the United States. Skin symptoms cannot diagnose it; reference amounts for ALA do not establish an EPA/DHA target.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: Omega-3 supplements can cause gastrointestinal and other adverse effects; source safety limits are not a personal dosing goal.
excess.medicalBoundary: No upper limit is an intake goal. Seek professional or medical advice before changing supplement or medication use.

interactions.counterparty: Medicines discussed in the linked NIH ODS fact sheet
interactions.description: High supplemental amounts can increase bleeding problems with warfarin or other anticoagulants; seek professional review.
interactions.limitations: Informational summary, not a complete interaction list or an instruction to change medicines.
